channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: Why apps now charge for AI: credits, usage packs and premium plans
item.description: AI features cost companies money every time you use them, so apps are moving from "free AI" to limits, credits and paid tiers, and this month brought several examples.

item.title: iPhone Duo after the first weeks: problems, settings and apps to know
item.description: Apple's first foldable iPhone has drawn complaints about cracking inner screens, Touch ID and settings you can only pick once, while a wave of small apps now uses its fold.

item.title: Scams going around this week: fake upgrades, fake invites, fake bills
item.description: This week's scams all copy a company you trust, a phone network, OpenAI or your internet provider, and push you to act fast; checking through the company's own app stops most of them.

item.title: ChatGPT Standard and Advanced Voice end on 11 December; Live replaces them
item.description: OpenAI is retiring ChatGPT's Standard and Advanced voice modes on 11 December. Anyone using either moves to Live, the voice mode OpenAI introduced in July.

item.title: Gemini on CarPlay: Google's AI app now talks with you while you drive
item.description: Google's Gemini app now works on Apple CarPlay, so you can have hands-free Gemini Live conversations in the car. It's rolling out worldwide from 11 November in every Gemini Live language.

item.title: Samsung: core Galaxy AI features stay free, some new ones may cost extra
item.description: Samsung told Tech Advisor its core Galaxy AI features will remain free, after a leak pointed to a $4.99-a-month Galaxy AI Premium plan. It said some advanced capabilities or new services may become paid options.

item.title: Revolut Pay now works on Uber in the UK and most of Europe
item.description: You can now pay for Uber rides and Uber Eats orders with Revolut Pay in the UK, Switzerland, Norway and most of the EU, and earn extra RevPoints on each one.

item.title: Apple Support Community forums close on 20 November
item.description: Apple's Support Community forums, where users help each other fix problems, stopped taking new posts and will close for good on 20 November. Apple didn't give a reason.

item.title: Google Fi now switches between two networks, fully on Pixel 9 and newer
item.description: Google Fi now uses two carriers' networks and switches phones to the stronger signal, calling it a "super network". Getting the full benefit needs a Pixel 9 or newer.

item.title: DuckDuckGo browser on Windows now supports Bitwarden and LastPass
item.description: DuckDuckGo's Windows browser now lets you add password manager extensions, starting with Bitwarden and LastPass. Mac support is in the works.

item.title: Blue Phone: a Pixel 10 Pro with an AI assistant that works across your apps
item.description: Startup Blue opened the public beta of Blue Phone, a Pixel 10 Pro or Pro XL running its own Blue OS, where an AI assistant does tasks across apps for you.

item.title: Jitless plays your PC and classic iOS games on iPhone and iPad
item.description: Jitless keeps your PC and classic iOS games in one library and lets you play them with touch, a controller or a keyboard and mouse. It was #8 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 11 November.

item.title: Offline AI Voice Translator translates speech without internet
item.description: Offline AI Voice Translator turns your speech into spoken translation without an internet connection once you've downloaded its AI model. It was #63 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 11 November.

item.title: Watchmen maps surveillance cameras and license plate readers near you
item.description: Watchmen shows public surveillance cameras on a map, including license plate readers, traffic and speed cameras. It was #20 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 11 November.

item.title: LayerLoops lets you draw shapes and record video inside them
item.description: LayerLoops is a camera app where you draw on the screen and record live video into what you drew, building a video out of layers. It was #33 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 11 November.

item.title: Font Shelf installs fonts you own on your iPhone and iPad
item.description: Font Shelf imports TrueType and OpenType fonts, even whole zip files, groups them by family and prepares a profile so iOS can install them. It was #40 among paid Graphics & Design apps on the US App Store on 11 November.

item.title: Shredder Weather forecasts snow at every ski area up to 15 days out
item.description: Shredder Weather is a snow forecast app for skiers and snowboarders, with a multi-model snowfall forecast for every ski area worldwide. It was #40 among free Weather apps on the US App Store on 11 November.

item.title: Pitch Mode presents slides from your iPhone with notes and a timer
item.description: Pitch Mode shows your slides on a TV or monitor while your iPhone or iPad keeps speaker notes, the next slide and a timer. It was #48 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 11 November.

item.title: Chrome zero-day: update Chrome now to fix a bug attackers already use
item.description: Google released a Chrome update that fixes nine security flaws, including one that attackers are already exploiting. It's the eighth such Chrome zero-day this year.

item.title: Spotify AI DJ: new voices and a setting for less talking
item.description: Spotify's AI DJ now lets Premium users pick from new voices with their own personalities, and switch off most of the talking between songs.

item.title: Claude Sheets and Whiteboards: Claude now builds spreadsheets and boards with you
item.description: Anthropic added Sheets and Whiteboards to Claude in beta, on all paid plans: Claude builds a spreadsheet or a shared brainstorming board with you and your team. Claude Dashboards is now generally available as Claude Data.

item.title: Samsung Gallery can now back up photos to Google Photos
item.description: Samsung's Gallery app now backs up photos and videos to Google Photos with a feature called Gallery Sync, replacing the old Microsoft OneDrive option. It needs One UI 9.

item.title: November Pixel Drop: Pixel Solver, Create My Widget and Gemini Call Screen
item.description: Google's November Pixel Drop started rolling out on 10 November to supported Pixel phones, tablets and watches. It adds an AI math solver to the Calculator, a widget builder you describe in words and Gemini Call Screen.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon now available more widely, in the Gemini app with AI Ultra
item.description: Google opened Gemini 4 Carbon, its model for complex coding and research, beyond the cybersecurity teams that got it first in October. In the Gemini app it's for Google AI Ultra subscribers, who pay $100 a month.

item.title: iPhone sandbox escape lets apps read other apps' files on iOS 26 and 27
item.description: Code published on GitHub, called worse_query, lets an app read other apps' files on iPhones with iOS 26 and 27. Binance warns it could expose crypto wallet keys and logins; Apple's latest updates don't list a fix.

item.title: PlayStation Plus PC app shuts down on 10 December
item.description: Sony is retiring the PlayStation Plus app for PC, which let Premium members stream PS5 games on a computer, on 10 December. Sony says fewer than 0.4% of eligible Premium members used it.

item.title: Reddit Reviews sums up what Reddit users say about a product
item.description: Reddit now turns its users' conversations about a product into a review page, with a summary of what people are saying and how many comments are positive, negative or mixed. It's live for all US users.

item.title: Apple TV adds sign language interpretation on 13 November
item.description: From Friday, 13 November, some Apple Original films in the Apple TV app can be watched with sign language interpretation, starting with Being Heumann. F1 gets both American and British Sign Language.

item.title: Ring Drone Cam: $249.99 indoor security drone ships 27 January
item.description: Amazon's Ring is selling the Drone Cam, a small indoor drone with cameras that patrols your home, for $249.99, shipping on 27 January 2027. Ring also announced the Rover Cam.

item.title: One UI 9.5 may let Galaxy phones record WhatsApp, Telegram and Meet calls
item.description: An early One UI 9.5 build has a "Record calls in other apps" option in Samsung's Phone app, with a switch each for WhatsApp, Telegram and Google Meet, SamMobile found.

item.title: Adobe MAX 2026: AI agents in Photoshop and Premiere, Acrobat in Google Drive
item.description: At Adobe MAX, Adobe added AI agents and new tools to Photoshop, Premiere, Lightroom and Firefly, and Google said Adobe Acrobat will open straight from Google Drive and Gmail.

item.title: DuoFridge turns your iPhone into a retro fridge with magnets and photos
item.description: DuoFridge lets you decorate a retro fridge with magnets and your photos and save it as a wallpaper. It was #2 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 10 November.

item.title: murmur daily sends three short messages a day matched to your mood
item.description: Each morning you tell murmur how you feel in one word, and it sends three short messages for that feeling: morning, midday and evening. It was #3 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 10 November.

item.title: Warhammer Survivors is out on iPhone, from the makers of Boltgun and Vampire Survivors
item.description: Warhammer Survivors, a survivors-style action game set in the Warhammer universes, launched on iPhone and was #3 among all paid apps on the US App Store on 10 November.

item.title: ReceiptLocker scans receipts and sorts them by tax category on your iPhone
item.description: ReceiptLocker reads the vendor, total and date from a receipt photo on your iPhone and files it in a category that follows the US Schedule C tax form. It was #41 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 10 November.

item.title: FieldKit puts offline AI, survival guides and maps on your iPhone
item.description: FieldKit gives you an AI that runs on your iPhone, 313 practical references and offline maps, so you can look things up without internet. It was #74 among paid Reference apps on the US App Store on 10 November.

item.title: Chord Lab turns your iPhone into a chord instrument with a joystick
item.description: Chord Lab gives you seven chord keys and a joystick to play chords, strums and arpeggios with 110 sounds. It was #11 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 10 November.

item.title: roam sets alarms that ring only when you're in that time zone
item.description: In roam, each alarm belongs to a time zone and rings only while your phone is there, so travel alarms switch on when you land and home alarms take over when you're back. It was #63 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 10 November.

item.title: Waze now warns drivers about nearby cyclists using Garmin LiveTrack
item.description: Cyclists who turn on Garmin LiveTrack on a Garmin bike computer or watch can choose to appear in Waze, and drivers get an alert when one is nearby.

item.title: iCloud outage on 10 November: Mail, sign-in and Find My hit, now fixed
item.description: Apple confirmed an outage on 10 November that stopped iCloud Mail and Apple Account sign-in for some users and slowed Find My. Apple said all services were working again the same evening.

item.title: Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery for 4.5 hours off the grid
item.description: SpaceX's Starlink Mini 2 puts the dish, Wi-Fi router and a battery in one laptop-sized device that runs up to 4.5 hours, longer with extra batteries swapped in.

item.title: Xfinity gives a free 2 Gbps speed boost for 15 days for GTA 6
item.description: Xfinity is giving eligible internet customers a free 15-day boost to up to 2 Gbps download speeds, as GTA 6 pre-loads need up to 212 GB.

item.title: iOS 27.2 new features: Messages, TV profiles, FaceTime and more
item.description: iOS 27.2 adds new features in six Apple apps: Suggested Actions in Messages, profiles in the TV app, Dual Capture in Group FaceTime, new lock settings in Home, and changes in Podcasts and Games.

item.title: Xfinity phishing email: how to tell it's fake and what to do
item.description: Fake Xfinity emails say a payment failed, your bill is suspended or a voicemail is waiting, with a link that looks like xfinity.com but ends on a scam page that asks for your login or card.

item.title: Samsung Keyboard may clean up your voice typing, like Pixel's Rambler
item.description: A One UI 9.5 test build has a Samsung Keyboard setting called Refine Voice Input that removes filler words and hesitations, with the text appearing after you finish speaking, SamMobile found.

item.title: How to check if an image is AI-generated on iPhone
item.description: Google's SynthID Detector can tell whether an image was made or edited with AI tools from companies that add the invisible SynthID watermark, including Apple, OpenAI, Google, Nvidia and Kakao.

item.title: iPadOS 27.3 beta: double-tap the top of a window to make it full screen
item.description: The iPadOS 27.3 beta adds a setting that lets you double-tap the top of an app window to zoom it to full screen, and double-tap again to go back.

item.title: Disney+ on Meta Quest now has 60+ 3D movies and themed screens
item.description: The updated Disney+ app on Meta Quest streams more than 60 movies in 3D, including The Avengers and Black Panther, for subscribers.

item.title: New Siri Remote: Precision Finding needs an iPhone 17 or newer
item.description: The new Siri Remote that comes with the Apple TV 4K on Friday can be found with Precision Finding, but only from an iPhone 17 or newer.

item.title: ChatGPT and Claude missed skin cancers on darker skin, study finds
item.description: In a study presented at a dermatology meeting, Claude and ChatGPT called 13 of 48 skin cancers on darker skin harmless with at least 70% confidence.
